subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood deployment options & urgent capacity issue
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fintechco.com>, Aarti Desai <aarti@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + deployment options / next steps

Hi Samir / Aarti,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- You showed the realtime fraud-check flow (~120 req/s peak today) and current pain points: bursty traffic during settlement windows and a single incident last week where your hosted endpoint hit quota limits and experienced throttling.
- Key requirements you called out: predictable sustained throughput, strict PII controls, and an on-call escalation path.

Deployment options we discussed:
1) Hosted API: fastest onboarding, lower TCO for smaller volumes, but shared capacity and default quotas.
2) Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with committed throughput; recommended when sustained QPS and predictable latency are required.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full isolation, customer-managed networking + KMS — typically for regulated PII-heavy flows.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm expected 99th percentile QPS and peak burst size (tokens/second) so Rishi can size a Dedicated pool.
- Send any incident logs (throttle/429 timestamps) so we can correlate.
- If you prefer, we can fast-track a Dedicated pilot with an SLA-backed window while legal/procurement works through the contract.

Can we aim for a quick alignment call tomorrow to decide if we should start Dedicated onboarding immediately? If this is urgent, flag here and I will loop in Vivek for executive prioritization.

Best,
Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

Laura — thanks for the summary. We're in an urgent spot: last Friday our hosted endpoint experienced sustained throttling during the 02:00 settlement window which caused ~8 minutes of failed enrichment calls. That translated to downstream batch retries and a delayed settlement. Our on-call team escalated to the vendor (your hosted endpoint) and it recovered after a quota bump, but this is not acceptable going forward.

Short answers to your questions:
- Expected sustained: 180 req/s during settlement windows (10–15 min), normal steady-state 40–60 req/s.
- Bursts: up to 400 req/s for 30–60s on heavy days.
- Logs: attaching a trimmed log with 429 timestamps.

We want to evaluate Dedicated immediately. Procurement is queued but we can get an internal signoff for a pilot if Redwood can commit to a clear onboarding timeline and temporary credit for the incident. Can you treat this as high priority?

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Integrations — FintechCo
samir@fintechco.com

Hi Samir — appreciate the quick turnaround and the logs. I pulled the 429 windows from the attachment and did a quick pass. A few notes and immediate mitigations:

- The pattern looks like prefix-bursting during settlement start; the hosted pool hit per-tenant connection limits.
- Immediate mitigation: we can apply a short-term quota increase and enable aggressive prefix KV caching for your common prompts to lower token usage. That will likely reduce pressure while we stand up Dedicated.
- For Dedicated sizing: given your sustained 180 req/s and 400 req/s bursts, I recommend a 2-GPU Reserved pool configured for continuous throughput with room for x2 burst via burst capacity.

Can you confirm: 1) timeline for procurement sign-off (even if provisional), 2) do you require VPC/private networking or is Dedicated with shared networking acceptable for now?

I'll draft an expedited onboarding checklist for the Dedicated pilot (expected spin-up 5–7 business days after contract + infra poke). If you need faster, we can discuss a warm-standby option — will escalate to Vivek for prioritization.

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Samir Shah <samir@fintechco.com>

Rishi — thanks, that plan sounds reasonable. A few clarifications: 
- Procurement: we can provisionally greenlight a pilot and provide PO within 3 business days if SOW and price are agreed. Final contract may take 2–3 weeks.
- Networking: Dedicated with shared networking is acceptable for the pilot. If we see PII concerns in the eval, we will escalate to Private VPC.
- Fast-track ask: we need the pilot up within 5 business days if possible. The settlement windows are every night and we can't risk another outage.

I've re-attached the log extract and a short summary from our infra on-call.

Samir
